questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Pfannenstiel incision is placed ______ and its features are ______.
opts: A finger-breadth above pubic symphysis (low transverse); cosmetically good, rectus muscle not cut
3 cm below the ASIS line; straight
questions.exp: Pfannenstiel: finger breadth above symphysis, cosmetic, rectus not cut. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Joel-Cohen incision differs from Pfannenstiel in being:
opts: Not curved and placed above Pfannenstiel (3 cm below the line joining both ASIS)
questions.exp: Joel-Cohen: straight, 3 cm below inter-ASIS line. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Advantages and disadvantage of transverse skin incision:
opts: Less post-op pain, greater wound strength, better cosmesis; upper abdomen not visualised
questions.exp: Advantages: less pain, stronger wound, cosmetic; disadvantage: upper abdomen not seen. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Match the uterine incision – Sanger's : Kerr's : Krönig's.
opts: Classical (upper segment vertical) : lower segment transverse (LSCS) : low vertical
questions.exp: Sanger = classical; Kerr = LSCS; Krönig = low vertical. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Risk of scar rupture – classical : one previous LSCS : multiple previous LSCS : low vertical.
questions.exp: Classical 4–9%; one LSCS 0.2–0.9%; multiple LSCS 0.9–1.8%; low vertical 1–7%. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: VBAC eligibility – classical : LSCS : low vertical (Krönig).
questions.exp: VBAC contraindicated after classical; ± after LSCS or low vertical (Krönig indicated for constriction ring). (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: After a classical C-section, the next pregnancy is managed by:
opts: Repeat C-section at 36–37 weeks (after 37 weeks contractions become prominent → ↑ rupture); the repeat should be LSCS
questions.exp: Repeat CS at 36–37 wks, done as LSCS. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Recommendations on VBAC after LSCS – ACOG : Indian national guidelines.
opts: VBAC may be tried irrespective of number of previous LSCS : VBAC contraindicated if ≥2 previous LSCS → C-section
VBAC after 1 only : VBAC after any number
questions.exp: ACOG: any number; national guidelines: ≥2 LSCS → repeat CS. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Options after a previous C-section and the success of trial of scar:
opts: Trial of scar/VBAC/TOLAC (successful → vaginal delivery in 70–72%; rupture → laparotomy; impending rupture → immediate CS) or repeat CS at 36–37 weeks
questions.exp: TOLAC succeeds 70–72%; uterine rupture → laparotomy; impending rupture → immediate CS; else repeat CS 36–37 wks. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Risks associated with trial of labour include increased:
opts: Bleeding, blood transfusion, uterine rupture, hysterectomy, fetal distress/death, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy
questions.exp: TOLAC risks: bleeding, transfusion, rupture, hysterectomy, fetal distress/death, HIE. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Risks associated with elective caesarean:
opts: Obstetric history affected, ↑ transient tachypnea of newborn, anaesthetic and operative risks
questions.exp: Elective CS: alters future obstetric history, TTN, anaesthetic/operative risk. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Risk of scar rupture depends on:
opts: Type of C-section, number of previous C-sections, inter-delivery interval
questions.exp: Type, number and inter-delivery interval. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Inter-delivery gap – ideal : 'short' interval : minimum gap between caesarean and next pregnancy.
questions.exp: Ideal ≥18 months; short = 12 months; minimum CS-to-conception gap 6 months. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Anaesthesia levels – epidural for painless labour : caesarean section.
questions.exp: Labour epidural T10; caesarean T4. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Ideal position for caesarean and timing of elective CS for non-medical reasons:
opts: Supine with 15° left lateral tilt or wedge under right hip; 39 weeks
questions.exp: 15° left tilt / wedge under right hip; elective CS at 39 weeks. (Book p564)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Absolute contraindications to VBAC include all EXCEPT:
opts: Previous classical CS, uterine rupture, myomectomy/hysterotomy, T-shaped incision, or incision extended into upper segment
Contracted pelvis, CPD in present pregnancy
Home delivery / no facility for emergency CS
questions.exp: Past h/o CPD is NOT a C/I; the others are. A T-shaped incision extends from LUS into upper segment. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Relative contraindications where repeat CS is preferred:
questions.exp: Relative: macrosomia, post-term, breech. Twins and polyhydramnios are NOT contraindications. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Prognostic markers for VBAC – most important favourable : bad marker.
opts: Previous history of vaginal delivery : h/o puerperal sepsis/endometritis after previous CS
questions.exp: Prior vaginal delivery is the best predictor; puerperal sepsis/endometritis after prior CS is a bad marker. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Monitoring during VBAC includes:
opts: Maternal pulse rate, CTG monitoring, scar tenderness
Serial USG for scar thickness every hour
questions.exp: Pulse, CTG, scar tenderness. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Induction of labour in a previous C-section is done by:
opts: Mechanical method for cervical ripening followed by oxytocin
questions.exp: IOL possible: mechanical ripening → oxytocin (PGs avoided). (Book p566)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: With a previous C-section – external podalic version : internal podalic version : contracted pelvis.
opts: Relative C/I : absolute C/I : recurrent indication for caesarean
questions.exp: External version relative C/I; internal podalic version absolute C/I; contracted pelvis is a recurrent CS indication. (Book p566)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Increased complications after caesarean include:
opts: Transient tachypnea of newborn and postpartum endometritis
questions.exp: TTN and postpartum endometritis. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Indications for classical caesarean section (difficult access to lower segment) include:
opts: Carcinoma cervix (absolute), dense uterus–bladder adhesions, placenta previa with large vessels over LUS, very early preterm CS (LUS not formed), perimortem CS
questions.exp: Classical CS: Ca cervix (absolute), dense adhesions, vascular previa, very early preterm, perimortem. (Book p565)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Perimortem caesarean section should be performed within:
questions.exp: Perimortem CS within 4 minutes. (Book p565)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: M/c anaesthesia for caesarean and the preferred option in heart disease/PIH:
questions.exp: Spinal is m/c; heart disease and PIH → neuraxial/epidural. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Indications for general anaesthesia in caesarean/obstetric procedures:
opts: Fetal distress, convulsions, manoeuvres needing a hand inside the uterus (internal podalic version, manual replacement of inverted uterus, manual removal of placenta)
questions.exp: GA: fetal distress, convulsions, intrauterine manipulation (IPV, inversion replacement, MRP). (Book p566)

units.title: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
units.guide: Place the Pfannenstiel and Joel-Cohen incisions, weigh transverse-incision pros and cons, and compare Sanger's, Kerr's and Krönig's uterine incisions by rupture risk and VBAC eligibility. Focus for this checkpoint: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section.

units.title: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
units.guide: Choose between TOLAC and repeat section, list the risks of each path, and master the inter-delivery interval numbers and anaesthesia levels. Focus for this checkpoint: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section.

units.title: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
units.guide: Separate absolute from relative contraindications to VBAC, remember what is NOT a contraindication, identify prognostic markers and monitor the scar. Focus for this checkpoint: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring.

units.title: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
units.guide: Know when the lower segment cannot be used, the 4-minute perimortem rule, and match spinal, epidural and general anaesthesia to their indications. Focus for this checkpoint: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean.
